items.title: Chuck Israels interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2021
items.q: the difference between Gershwin and Arlen, Frank Loesser, Cole Porter, and Andrew Lloyd Weber, there’s a chasm

ctx.x: Okay. So I’m happy. Okay a couple of things to wrap up with. You know usually when I get ready for an interview or most interviewers they do their homework and they might pick four or five topics that they definitely want to get to in the time they have. But those are not always the topics that the interviewees might pick. So I’m wondering if there’s something that you would like to talk about that I haven’t asked or that no one else has ever asked?

Well not that no one else has ever asked, but something I think about all the time is the discontinuity of musical language that happened roughly in the late 60s. And it happened not only in jazz it happened in popular music, it happened in theater music. You know the difference between Gershwin and Arlen, Frank Loesser, Cole Porter, and Andrew Lloyd Weber, there’s a chasm, an absolute chasm. All the rest is continuous music from pre- Bach, through Baroque classical romantic twentieth century music and the…
Could it have anything to do with technology?
